claim: vLLM 0.30.0 was qualified on this laptop (WSL2, RTX 5090 Laptop GPU 24GB) as a drop-in candidate for the production Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16 embedder (vLLM 0.25.0), then switched into production by a systemd --user drop-in that changes only the ExecStart binary path and PATH. Of the six qualification gates: (a) gate-text cosine, (c) batch invariance and (e) ai-memory vector reconstruction passed their pass bars; (b) mini-corpus retrieval and (d) live-code-index retrieval met top-10 SET identity on every query and trial (b: 40/40, d: 20/20 query-trials) but failed their strict top-10 ORDER bar in 3 of 4 trials each; (f) latency is report-only, with no pass bar. A prod-vs-prod control run (candidate never started) shows the same order-swap behavior already exists in production alone: gate b had 6 of 50 mismatched query-trials for the candidate (including an earlier, superseded run) against 10 of 80 for production compared with itself; gate d had 3 of 20 against 4 of 40; production against itself even had a worse single trial (6 of 10 identical) than any candidate trial. Gate (c)'s batch-invariance minimum cosine (0.9999562552851937) was bit-for-bit identical between production alone and the candidate, on the same minimizing text. The production switch itself re-checked only 30 gate texts (cosine 0.9999999999999998 before vs after) and confirmed dependents (ai-memory's vector stream, SocratiCode search); it did not re-run a post-switch top-10 retrieval check.
limitations: One host (laptop, RTX 5090 Laptop GPU 24GB, WSL2) and one model/route (/v1/embeddings with Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16); not a claim about other GPUs, models or the /v2/embed route. NVIDIA's model card still names vllm==0.25.0 for BF16 /v2/embed serving.

Retrieval equality covers 30 gate texts (a), a 50-paragraph mini-corpus over 10 queries (b), and 5 live code-index queries (d), not an aggregate retrieval-quality benchmark. Gates b and d met top-10 content-SET identity on every query and trial (b: 40/40 query-trials across the 4 recorded trials, plus full set overlap on one earlier superseded run; d: 20/20 query-trials) but did not meet strict top-10 ORDER identity on every trial (that earlier superseded run's own order count was 9 of 10). Counting every recorded run: gate b had 6 of 50 candidate query-trials with an order mismatch against 10 of 80 for a prod-vs-prod control (candidate never started, run twice -- an earlier, superseded control and the current one -- both included since only the second run's own prod_score diagnostic sub-field needed a fix, not its order counts); gate d had 3 of 20 against 4 of 40. Production compared with itself had a worse single trial (6 of 10 identical, i.e. 4 mismatched) than any candidate trial (worst: 7 of 10 identical, 3 mismatched), so this order-swap behavior is pre-existing production batching noise, not attributable to the 0.30.0 upgrade. The swap-gap range is 3.5e-05 to 8.2e-04 across all 23 recorded swaps (candidate run and both control runs combined), far smaller than the ~0.02-0.05 gaps between other adjacent ranks in the same rankings.

The reference receipt's own qualification-time number for this style of check (mini_corpus_top10_overlap, '10/10 on each of 10 queries') is a content-SET overlap claim, not a strict-order claim; it does not report whether its own order matched on every query, so gate (b)'s order tracking here is additional detail, not a comparison against a reported order result. The reference receipt's one reported ORDER number (production_switch.code_queries_identical_top10_order, '5/5') comes from its own post-switch production check with 5 live code queries, a different procedure from this run's own gate (d) qualification check (5 queries against the live SocratiCode index, run before any switch); the two are not directly comparable, and this run made no post-switch top-10 check of its own (see production_switch below: only 30 gate texts and a cosine value were re-checked after the switch) -- unlike the reference, which also re-checked 5 code queries' top-10 order after its own switch (that same code_queries_identical_top10_order, '5/5').

0.30.0 relies on its pinned-memory fallback for WSL (vllm-project/vllm PR #56908, the same warning the reference receipt's owned instance logged); the 0.29.0 UVA failure recorded in vllm-compatibility remains true for 0.29.0.
The 0.25.0 unit is kept for rollback; only a drop-in override (nemotron-embed-agent-lab.service.d, ExecStart and PATH only) points production at 0.30.0.

A diagnostic-only bug in this run's own gate (b) script (prod_scores_by_idx had score and index reversed) made the order_diff_detail[].prod_score sub-field in every candidate-vs-prod gate (b) file (gate_b_result.json and gate_b_trial{1,2,3}.json) and in the first, superseded prod-vs-prod control unreliable; it did not affect any cosine value, top-10 set, or pass/fail boolean -- only that one diagnostic sub-field -- and was fixed before the second, current prod-vs-prod control run. See raw/ERRATUM-gate_b-order_diff_detail-prod_score-bug.txt.

candidate_isolated_instance.isolation_proof: Identical to prod's own /proc/<PID>/exe target. This is expected, not a leak: both vllm-0.25.0/bin/python and vllm-0.30.0/bin/python are uv-managed symlinks to the SAME shared base CPython interpreter (verified via ls -la on both venvs' bin/python). control_prod_vs_prod.purpose: Determine whether the top-10 order swaps seen candidate-vs-prod in gates (b) and (d) are request-level batching/numeric noise already present when production is compared against itself, or specific to the 0.25.0-vs-0.30.0 comparison.
control_prod_vs_prod.method: Both sides of gates (b) and (d) pointed at production 127.0.0.1:8231 (vLLM 0.25.0); the candidate (38231) was NOT started for this control. Same corpus, same queries, same gate texts, same batching pattern as the original candidate-vs-prod runs (each trial = one separate top-level script invocation issuing separate HTTP requests per trial). There were two separate control runs (the first, superseded one and the current one below), each with its own 4 trials for (b) and (d) and its own gate (c) batch-invariance run against production alone (8 b/d trials and 2 gate-c runs in total).

first_superseded_run.note: This run's own order_diff_detail[].prod_score sub-field for gate (b) carries the same reversed-dict bug described in the erratum (it predates the fix), so its diagnostic gap values for gate (b) are not used; its order COUNTS (from queries_with_identical_order / queries_identical_count, a different, unaffected code path) are valid and reported below. Gate (d)'s diagnostic (order_diff_score_gap_prod) never had this bug, so this run's gate (d) gap values are used directly.

current_run.note: Generated after the erratum fix; both gate (b) and gate (d) diagnostic sub-fields are reliable in this run.

totals.gate_b: candidate: 6 mismatched query-trials of 50 (5 trials x 10 queries: the 4 recorded trials plus the one earlier superseded run). production-vs-production (both control runs combined, 8 trials x 10 queries): 10 mismatched query-trials of 80. Production compared with itself had a worse single trial (6 of 10 identical, i.e. 4 mismatched, first-superseded-run trial 2) than any candidate trial (worst: 7 of 10 identical, 3 mismatched).
totals.gate_d: candidate: 3 mismatched query-trials of 20 (4 trials x 5 queries). production-vs-production (both control runs combined, 8 trials x 5 queries): 4 mismatched query-trials of 40.
totals.swap_gap_range_all_runs: 3.5e-05 to 8.2e-04 across all 23 recorded swaps (candidate run and both control runs combined). Gate (d)'s own order_diff_score_gap_prod diagnostic was never affected by the erratum and is used throughout. Gate (b)'s per-query order_diff_detail.prod_score is only usable where it postdates the erratum fix (the current control run); the earlier superseded run's own gap (0.00018, from raw/gate_b_near_tie_diagnostic_run1.txt, a separate script that never went through the buggy code path) is used for that one run instead. The other 13 gate (b) swaps (candidate trials 1-3 and the superseded control run) use the candidate-side score, which the erratum never affected. All 23 swaps are single adjacent-rank swaps and fall inside the stated range.

control_prod_vs_prod.conclusion: The top-10 order swaps observed candidate-vs-prod in gates (b) and (d) are NOT specific to vLLM 0.30.0: running the identical gates with BOTH sides on production alone (across two separate control runs) reproduces order swaps at a comparable or worse rate (gate b: 10/80 mismatched query-trials prod-vs-prod against 6/50 for the candidate, with production's own worst single trial, 6/10 identical, worse than the candidate's worst trial, 7/10 identical; gate d: 4/40 against 3/20) and the same tiny score-gap magnitude (3.5e-05 to 8.2e-04 throughout). Gate (c)'s batch-invariance minimum cosine is bit-for-bit IDENTICAL between production alone and the candidate (0.9999562552851937, same minimizing text in both), showing the batching-induced floating-point noise floor is a property already present in production's own request-level batching, unchanged by the 0.30.0 upgrade. This directly answers the coordinator's question: the order-swap noise is pre-existing production batching noise, not a 0.30.0 regression.
control_prod_vs_prod.erratum: A diagnostic-only bug in scripts/gate_b_retrieval.py's order_diff_detail[].prod_score field (a reversed score->index dict instead of index->score) made that one sub-field unreliable in every candidate-vs-prod gate (b) file and in the first, superseded prod-vs-prod control run; it did not affect any cosine value, top-10 set, or pass/fail boolean, and was fixed before the second, current control run. See raw/ERRATUM-gate_b-order_diff_detail-prod_score-bug.txt.
